status: AUTHORITATIVE. Supersedes any prose or model-memory summary of the method.
why: A fresh context summarised the method as 'MMD over Adam-preconditioned gradients', which omits that TARGET gradients are SGD while CANDIDATE gradients are Adam-aware. Implementing from that summary would have produced a different experiment.

frozen_feature_contract.emphasis: candidate and target gradient types DIFFER (adam vs sgd). This asymmetry is part of the frozen protocol and must be preserved for the BBH round.

candidate_cache.reuse_policy: REUSED VERBATIM. Candidate gradients are target-independent, so the BBH round must not regenerate them; only target/query gradients are new.
candidate_cache.hash_convention: sha256 of TENSOR CONTENT (v.numpy().tobytes()), matching `tsha` in build_targetdraw_master_manifest.py — NOT the file bytes.

warmup_checkpoint.why_optimizer_matters: Adam preconditioning of candidate gradients reads exp_avg / exp_avg_sq from this checkpoint; a drifted optimizer.pt changes the candidate feature space without changing any config.

dsmc.must_not_use: the generic online MMDSelector in src/dataflex/train/selector/mmd_selector.py — its target_gradient_type defaults to 'same', which would make target gradients Adam-aware and would NOT be the frozen DSMC

less.must_not_use: official trajectory-LESS; this arm is the relevance-topk reimplementation

first_rr.kernel: greedy round-robin over queries, s = <x, t>

second_rr.kernel: greedy round-robin over queries, s = <x, t>^2
second_rr.note: SAME script and SAME rr_perm_seed as first_rr; only the representation order differs

randk.exact_procedure: N = candidate_cache.shape[0]; g = torch.Generator().manual_seed(random_k_seed); indices = torch.randperm(N, generator=g)[:K].tolist()
randk.note: plain uniform Random-K on a CPU torch.Generator, bit-reproducible. NOT select_randk_lenmatch.py — randk_lenmatch was an MMLU-only 9th arm and is NOT part of the 5-method BBH set.

llamafactory_preprocessing_pin.why: infer_seqlen decides the source/target budget split; supervised.py applies source_ids[:source_len] (tail truncation); template.py defines the llama2 [INST] wrapper. All three determine what the query gradient is actually taken on.

target_gradient_extraction.driver: dataflex-cli train <select yaml> (target-only phase), as in run_targetdraw_pilot.sh
target_gradient_extraction.lora_dropout_WARNING: TARGET-GRADIENT EXTRACTION uses lora_dropout=0.1 and downstream selected-data SFT uses 0.05. These are DIFFERENT ON PURPOSE and must not be unified. 0.1 is the historical value every completed MMLU target-gradient config used, so changing it would make BBH target gradients incomparable to the MMLU arm. A future reader who sees 'the audited correct dropout is 0.05' in resolved_run_provenance.json must NOT propagate that to the extraction config: 0.05 is the SFT value.
target_gradient_extraction.cutoff_len_rationale: RAISED from 2048 to 3072 for target-gradient extraction ONLY (decision in code_review_0810_2). 3072 = Llama-2 context 4096 minus the pinned max_gen_toks 1024, i.e. the evaluation side's own input ceiling; measured max BBH eval context is 2569. At 2048, 7/192 query records lost their own query and CoT cue (source-tail truncation). Protocol-derived, NOT accuracy-tuned: no BBH accuracy has been observed.
target_gradient_extraction.sft_cutoff_note: downstream selected-data SFT recipe is UNCHANGED at 2048
target_gradient_extraction.differs_from_mmlu_arm: yes, deliberately: the MMLU arm used 2048 for query gradients. Disclosed as a pre-compute validity correction.
target_gradient_extraction.candidate_symlink_rule: the per-draw cache's train/1/all_projected_grads.pt must be a symlink resolving to the frozen candidate cache; verify with readlink -f before selection
target_gradient_extraction.CANARY_MUST_LOG: during the selection canary, log the ACTUALLY LOADED PEFT config dropout and the model.training flag. If LoRA dropout is active during gradient extraction, repeat draw0 target extraction once from a clean cache and compare the projected-gradient tensor hash: 64 targets is cheap, and non-reproducible target gradients would undermine every downstream selection hash. If dropout is inactive (eval mode, or overridden by the loaded adapter config), record that instead.
target_gradient_extraction.HOW_TO_APPLY_THE_CUTOFF: Use EXACT_SETUP_COMMAND above -- all four arguments are required. The script's defaults are the MMLU ones (target_draws/<draw>.jsonl, cutoff 2048, no verification), and there is NO data/target_draws/bbhx_draw*.jsonl, so a bare invocation aborts with the correct command printed rather than silently using the wrong input or cutoff. The script fail-loud verifies the prompt sha256 against bbh_query_prompt_manifest.json, the 64-row count, the ordered-id hash against the frozen draw, rejects symlinks, and READS BACK the emitted YAML to confirm cutoff_len=3072 and lora_dropout=0.1.
target_gradient_extraction.TRUNCATION_GATE: bbh_token_truncation_audit.json MUST report verdict=PASS before any target-gradient extraction. At cutoff_len=3072 it reports PASS with 192/192 records retaining the complete query, CoT cue and supervised target, and 0 tokens dropped.

no_compute_run: artifacts only: no gradients, no selection, no SFT
